chunks: 333 - Ibn Abi Jayyid narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said:

Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) wrote to the Shia in Baghdad, al-Mada'in, al-Sawad, and the surrounding areas: I have appointed Abu Ali ibn Rashid in the place of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Abd Rabbih and those before him from my representatives, and I have made obedience to him equivalent to my obedience, and disobedience to him equivalent to my disobedience, and I wrote this in my own handwriting.

key_terms.أَبُو عَلِيٍّ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ: Abu Ali ibn Rashid, the appointed successor

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam al-Askari appoint as his successor and what is the status of his obedience?
ai.summary: This decree from Imam al-Askari (a.s.) to the Moalis in Baghdad and surrounding regions formally elevated Abu Ali ibn Rashid to the rank of his successor among the deputies, a critical step in the transition from the Minor to the Major Occultation. By declaring that obedience to him is legally equivalent to obedience to the Imam himself, the text establishes the principle of *al-wilayah al-tabi'ah* (subordinate guardianship), ensuring continuity of religious authority during the Imam's absence.
